newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends higher on oil/meal spreading.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends higher on oil/meal spreading.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended higher on Wednesday, boosted by oil/meal spreading amid expectations for a cutback in the weekly crush, traders said.

"It was an oil versus meal day," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "The liquidation was in the meal, oil settled higher. If we indeed are cutting the weekly crush, that can only be supportive to soyoil."
Soymeal closed $3.20 per ton lower to $0.70 higher with May down $3.20 at $279.60. Soyoil ended up 0.25 to 0.17 cent per lb with May up 0.17 at 24.17.
Unwinding of bull spreads pressured old crop soymeal contracts most of the session.
The July/December spread closed at $56.90, premium July, down $2.40 from Tuesday's close.
Traders pointed to a shift in floor sentiment from a bullish mood, tied to tight U.S. soybean stocks and strong world demand, to a bearish one.
They cited ideas USDA would not cut ending soybean stocks in Friday's Supply and Demand Report and indications world buyers were increasingly relying on South American supplies.
Analysts expected soybean stocks to fall only slightly in Friday's USDA Supply and Demand Report.

The soycomplex rallied last week, in part due to ideas USDA would slice 22 million bushels off the 1996-97 soybean ending stocks figure following last week's 22 million bushel downward revision in quarterly stocks.
Talk South Korea was retendering for South American soymeal also lent bearish ideas, traders said.
On the day, funds sold at least 1,000 lots of soymeal. Rosenthal Collins sold 500 May and 300 July, SAK Future sold 300 May and Smith Barney sold 200 July, pit sources said.
In soyoil, ADM bought 500 lots May and Cargill Inc bought 200 May and 300 July but sold 450 July.
Dean Witter sold 300 lots July and bought 200 May.
In spread trade, Iowa Grain spread 250 lots July/May soymeal at $2.70 to $2.80, premium July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 27,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 22,963 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 18,000 lots, against Tuesday's 11,916.
